compiled_state.description:
## Decision needed (not an implementation ticket yet)

`steep-tired-whimbrel` (f5c4-b2d1-4503-4bfe) was filed with an acceptance criterion requiring the
opt-in `verify.*` review gates to **fail CLOSED** on an unreadable config. That criterion was
deliberately NOT implemented, and left unticked, because the evidence gathered while fixing the
ticket's other half contradicts it. This ticket carries the decision so it is not silently dropped.

## The evidence AGAINST flipping to fail-closed

1. **It is the documented contract.** `docs/plan-review-gate.md:948-949`: "An unreadable config fails
   this opt-in gate *off* with a warning (it never auto-enables across a repo)." Flipping it breaks a
   live documented behaviour.
2. **A fail-closed gate here cannot actually run.** Measured counterfactual: with an unreadable config
   and the gate forced active, `close_plan_review_gate_check` returns
   `ok=False verdict='unavailable' reason='could not verify the plan-review attestation locally'` —
   the same unreadable config makes the attestation unreadable. Fail-closed buys zero enforcement and
   costs a hard block.
3. **Blast radius.** All three call sites hard-block: `claim` + `transition open->in_progress`, the
   plan-review close, and the completion close (which would additionally fire a billable LLM verifier
   whose own `llm.*` config is in the same unreadable file). One malformed character stops all work.
4. **All three keys default `false`**, so fail-closed would newly block repos that never enabled any
   gate — inverting the default for the majority to protect a minority it cannot actually protect.
5. **Precedent:** `cautious-defamatory-verdin` amended its AC to refuse a fail-fast for exactly this
   reason ("would convert a 2.1-hour hang into a HARD FAILURE of every attested gate run ... CI included").

## The evidence FOR revisiting it anyway

`gate_enabled`'s fail-open rationale had three legs, and **leg 2 was silently deleted**:
"the stronger signature gate fail-CLOSES independently". `soppy-petit-alleycat` (28f1-0ef8-65a4-4943)
retired `require_signature_for_close` on 2026-07-13 without updating the consumer that named it as its
safety net. Whimbrel corrected the stale docstring and the matching stale claim in `docs/config.md`,
but correcting the *documentation* of a compensating control is not the same as deciding whether the
posture still holds without it. Legs 1 and 3 survive and were judged sufficient — that judgement is
what this ticket exists to confirm or overturn.

## What is being asked

An operator ruling on ONE question: **do the opt-in `verify.*` gates keep failing OPEN on an unreadable
config?** Whimbrel made the two states distinguishable at the source, so either answer is now cheap to
implement per-caller with no second config read. If the answer is "keep fail-open", close this as
`not_a_bug` and the documented contract stands. If it is "flip it", this becomes an implementation
ticket and `docs/plan-review-gate.md` + `docs/config.md` must change with the code.

## Provenance
Deferred AC2 of `steep-tired-whimbrel`. Full argument, the runtime counterfactual, and the citations
are in that ticket's RCA, decision, and addendum comments.
compiled_state.title: Operator ruling: should the opt-in verify.* gates keep failing OPEN on an unreadable config?
